info.title: TeleWhatsApp control API
info.description: This document describes every operation of the whatsapp-api library and whatsapp-cli. The x-transport field indicates whether an operation is served by whatsapp-cli serve over HTTP today or invoked through the CLI. The x-cli field gives the exact command. The x-library field names the Rust entry points behind each operation (crate path form); the whatsapp-cli test `openapi_library_symbols_exist` verifies they exist. The x-live field marks operations that contact WhatsApp servers and require explicit authorization via --allow-live-request. The HTTP control plane has no authentication and binds to loopback only.

Blocked.description: Operation blocked by server refusal, cooldown or preserved state

PhoneNumber.description: Structured phone number with country code and national components

Jid.description: WhatsApp JID (Jabber ID) in form username@s.whatsapp.net for direct chats or username@g.us for groups

RequestId.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key; repeating the same request_id returns the saved outcome locally and never resends

Ok.description: Successful local-only mutation with no richer result

ActionStatus.description: Status of a queued action transmission

SendStatus.description: Status and state of a sent message

SendTicket.description: Ticket issued for a queued message

to.description: Direct recipient: E.164 digits, a `…@s.whatsapp.net` JID, or a `…@lid` JID. Omit when `group` is set. The LID form exists because a LID-addressed chat encrypts under a LID Signal address, which needs to be testable outside a group fan-out.

group.description: Group chat JID (`…@g.us`) for a sender-key fan-out send. Mutually exclusive with `to`; text only so far. lab-transport resolves the membership with a `w:g2` info query, the members' devices with `usync devices`, then addresses every device individually.

fresh_sessions.description: Discard the saved Signal session with each recipient device and establish a new one from a fresh prekey bundle, keeping the pinned peer identity (a changed identity is still refused). Applies to both the direct and the group fan-out path. Only legitimate with positive evidence that the peer never received what was encrypted under the old session.

skdm_delivery.description: Group send only: how the sender key is distributed. `participants` (default) puts one `<enc>` per device inside the group stanza's `<participants>`; `direct` sends one ordinary direct message per device carrying the distribution, before the group stanza, and omits `<participants>` entirely. Both are real — `includeSenderKeysInMessage` is a per-send flag in SendE2EMessageJob and SendLiveLocationKeyJob distributes keys entirely out of band.

image.description: Path to a PNG image file to send

voice_note.description: Path to an Ogg/Opus audio file to send as a voice note

view_once.description: If true, image is sent as view-once (disappears after one viewing)

status.description: Post a status instead of sending to a chat; mutually exclusive with `to` and `group`

quote.description: Reply to, or react to, an existing message in the group named by `group`

MessageRequest.description: Private JSON message request for outbox-send or lab-transport --message. Exactly one target: `to` (direct), `group` (sender-key fan-out) or `status` (a status post). Repeating the same request_id returns the saved outcome locally and never resends.

LabRegistrationConfig.description: Lab registration configuration template. The default recipe (body_mode enc_empty_h, client.user_agent 'WhatsApp/2.26.37.70 Android/unknown Device/unknown-unknown', and recommended code fields) is now provided by lab-signup template (GET /v1/signup/template). logo_entry.description: Internal APK material entry identifier for logo (debug only)

signature_entry.description: Internal APK material entry identifier for signature (debug only)

DerivedToken.description: Derived registration token from APK material. Token is base64-encoded and phone-bound; store it securely.

matches.description: True if the token in the config matches the derived token; false otherwise

TokenVerification.description: Verification result comparing a saved token to freshly derived material. Token value is never printed; only the match status is reported.

AppStatePatchRequest.description: Outgoing w:sync:app:state patch request (comparison 2.26.37.71 CSe.A00/CSe.A01). Library-level only: built and offline-verified, not yet queued by any command and never sent. x-transport is deliberately empty until a CLI or route exposes it.

collection.description: Collection name (LX/0oP.A03, confirmed). Which collection a given action belongs to is NOT decided here and is currently unknown; the caller supplies it.

order.description: 1 for critical_unblock_low, 0 otherwise (inferred from the CSe.A01 branch; the attribute's meaning was not traced).

version.description: The version this patch claims: the collection's current version plus one. Both our verifier and the server require patches to be strictly sequential.

return_snapshot.description: Emitted only when true. When the server sets it is untraced.

patch.description: SyncdPatch wire bytes from CollectionState::build_patch: version, mutations, snapshotMac, patchMac and a nested Blob keyId.

TextStyle.description: Colour and font of a styled full-screen text status, decoded from extendedTextMessage (LX/BZF descriptor, confirmed). All fields absent for an ordinary chat message. Carried on MessageContent::Text in the event journal.

background_argb.description: backgroundArgb, field 8, FIXED32 on the wire (unsigned, 4 bytes little-endian — NOT a varint int32). ARGB with alpha most significant.

text_argb.description: textArgb, field 7, FIXED32 on the wire. ARGB with alpha most significant.

font.description: font, field 9. Enum LX/C44 covers exactly wire values 0..=8; anything else is dropped rather than mapped.

audience.description: Identities allowed to see it (phone-number or LID form). Explicit because a status has no membership list and this client does not sync the account's status privacy list — this is WhatsApp's "share with only…".

background.description: Background colour as ARGB hex, with or without a leading #

text_color.description: Text colour as ARGB hex, with or without a leading #

StatusPost.description: A styled text status. Posted through the same sender-key fan-out as a group message, addressed to status@broadcast, with no addressing_mode and no phash (neither is observed on an incoming status).

status_id.description: The status we posted, by wire id

kind.description: Delivered (receipt with no type), Read (viewed), Played (video watched or voice heard)

StatusReceipt.description: One viewer's report about one of our statuses. Observed shape: `<receipt from=<viewer> [type]><participants message_id=<status id>/></receipt>` — the status is named by the participants child, not the receipt's own id. Recorded only; this client sends no read receipts of its own.

status_id.description: The status reacted to, by wire id

emoji.description: The emoji; null is a reaction being removed, recorded rather than dropped so a like does not appear to persist forever

StatusLike.description: A like on one of our statuses. A status reaction is an ordinary Message.reactionMessage (field 46) whose key names status@broadcast as the remoteJid — that is what distinguishes it from a chat reaction. In the APK it lands in status_add_on with type = 1, which a trigger counts into status_interactions.reaction_count.

message_id.description: Wire id of the message replied to or reacted to

participant.description: Who sent it. A group message id means nothing without this — the same id from two members is two different messages.

emoji.description: React with this emoji instead of replying; an empty string removes a previous reaction, which is a real operation and not the same as absent

quoted_text.description: The quoted message's own text, carried as quotedMessage. Absent quotes an empty body rather than inventing one.

QuotedTarget.description: An existing group message to reply to or react to. A reply carries `text` and no emoji; a reaction carries an emoji and no body — a reaction with a body, or a reply without one, renders as something else entirely on the recipient.

post.summary: Decrypt captured direct replies locally, without network I/O
post.description: Decrypt authenticated incoming records locally. The operation is offline. With `inspect: true`, display the plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. With replay_captures, preserved message captures are re-run through inbox::process offline to recover stanzas that an earlier defect refused; this is how the first live group messages were recovered after the sender-key distribution field number was corrected.

inspect.description: Inspect saved plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. Also prints, per preserved capture, the stanza tag/type, attribute names, enc child v/type values, and how the receive path would route it (from/participant server kinds and whether it routes as a group). Cleared and consumed rows are skipped rather than failing the run. Also prints the per-class counts on offline/offline_preview stanzas (message, receipt, status, notification, appdata, call), which is how to tell whether the server ever queued a given class of stanza for this account at all.

replay_captures.description: Re-run preserved incoming message captures through the normal receive path, offline. The server delivers a queued stanza once, so a stanza refused by a since-fixed guard is only recoverable from its capture. Already-committed messages dedupe; nothing is transmitted and no receipt is sent.

get.description: Returns the list of queued explicit receipts and their outcomes. The operation is offline and response content is redacted.

post.summary: Queue explicit read receipts for authenticated incoming messages (offline; the next `listen` session sends them once)
post.description: Durably queue read receipts for incoming messages. The operation is offline and returns immediately; a later session transmits them.

id.description: One or more incoming message ids as shown by `events`

post.summary: Start or resume a registration attempt
post.description: Initiates a WhatsApp registration flow for the given phone number. Returns 501 NotImplemented on the primary profile; use the lab flow (`/v1/signup/*`) for working registration.

get.summary: Show the current registration attempt
get.description: Retrieves the current registration attempt state.

delete.summary: Discard a completed or blocked attempt (local only)
delete.description: Resets the registration state and discards any completed or blocked attempt. This operation is local only.

post.summary: Reconcile an attempt whose request outcome was lost
post.description: Reconciles a registration attempt when the server response was not received locally, by querying the server for the actual status.

get.summary: Registration wire protocol profile
get.description: Returns wire-protocol profile for registration layer.

post.summary: One comparison-server connection; optional bounded primary login
post.description: Establish a single connection to the comparison server (x-live) with optional bounded primary login, message transmission, or receive mode. A successful login records this account's own LID from the `<success>` stanza, which a LID-addressed group names us by. When the message JSON carries `group` instead of `to`, the send is a sender-key fan-out: a `w:g2` info query resolves the membership, a `usync devices` query resolves each member's devices, `encrypt` supplies bundles for devices without a session, and one `<message>` carries a per-device `<enc>` distribution inside `<participants>` beside the group `skmsg`. It refuses rather than sending when a member has no device list. After any send the connection is held briefly and whatever the server sends next is preserved, because a recipient that cannot decrypt answers with a `receipt type="retry"` naming the failing device. A `<success>` or `<failure>` login result is preserved too: a `<failure>` carries an `appeal_token` and a refusal cannot be replayed to fetch one again.

login.description: Send one primary login after certificate verification

receive.description: Preserve incoming stanzas for up to 30 seconds without sending a chat

media_route.description: Obtain and privately preserve one current media-upload route response

message.description: Private JSON: request_id, either to (direct) or group (`…@g.us` fan-out), and text, image (PNG) or voice_note (Ogg/Opus); a group send is text only so far

recheck_refusal.description: Authorize exactly one further login after a saved `failure`, to tell a temporary limit from a permanent refusal. Requires a saved `failure` (never an ambiguous `outcome_unknown`), refuses to carry a message, and preserves the earlier refusal under its own key instead of overwriting it.

post.summary: Maintain an authenticated comparison connection and process incoming messages
post.description: Establish an authenticated session to the messaging server (x-live). Hold the connection for the requested duration, receive incoming messages, and optionally transmit all eligible queued intents. Group messages (enc type=skmsg) are decrypted when a SenderKeyDistributionMessage for the (group, sender) pair has been received in a prior or current direct message; messages without a stored sender key are preserved as Unsupported without acknowledgement. SKDM distribution arrives embedded in pkmsg/msg payloads (WhatsApp Message field 2), either standalone or as a second enc child of the group stanza, and is committed atomically with the inbox row. A decrypted group message is confirmed with a receipt addressed to the group carrying the sender as participant. Status updates (from=status@broadcast) route through the same sender-key path and project into a Broadcast chat with the poster as sender, but are never confirmed with a receipt: the status receipt shape (class=status, type=sender) has an unresolved sts input, so none is sent.

seconds.description: Stop after this many seconds; zero waits for Ctrl-C

send_outbox.description: Also transmit every eligible queued outbox intent, from any namespace, during this session. Inspect `outbox-pending` first.

put.summary: Queue the account-wide default disappearing timer for new chats
put.description: Queue the account-wide default disappearing timer for new chats (`xmlns=disappearing_mode` IQ); a live session transmits it.

post.summary: Request a code or resume an existing attempt; no automatic retries
post.description: Initiates or resumes a registration attempt. Requests a verification code via the specified method (sms or voice). Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: Inspect consent selectors once using saved identity; no OTP or SMS
post.description: Retrieves consent selectors for the current registration attempt without requiring OTP or SMS verification. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: Submit one reviewed decision from private JSON matching saved selectors
post.description: Submits a consent decision that matches the previously inspected selectors. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One additive-code-field experiment from a private EndpointFields JSON file
post.description: Sends an additive-code-field experiment using ENC plus empty H. Rejects replacement of saved fields. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One authorized repeat of HTTP 200 / bad_param to collect field hints
post.description: Repeats the request after a bad_param response to collect field hints. Same saved payload and keys. Durable latch prevents another repeat. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One encrypted-envelope experiment after HTTP 200 / bad_param
post.description: Sends an encrypted envelope after a bad_param response. Same inner fields and identity; no attestation, no automatic repeats. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One explicit post-failure reason/metrics experiment, using ENC plus empty H
post.description: Sends an explicit post-failure reason/metrics experiment using ENC plus empty H. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One authorized resend of a legacy refusal whose diagnostics were lost
post.description: Resends a legacy refusal whose diagnostics were lost. Known refusals and cooldowns are excluded. Durable latch prevents repeats. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One APK unknown-build-properties User-Agent experiment with additive fields
post.description: Sends an APK unknown-build-properties User-Agent experiment with additive fields. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One ENC plus empty-H experiment; does not fabricate attestation
post.description: Sends an encrypted envelope with empty hash. Does not fabricate attestation. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: Ask the server to email the one-time code to the address on file
post.description: Requests the server to email the one-time code to the registered email address. Uses /v2/code with method=email_otp. Optional email parameter is rejected when given. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

email.description: Email address (not sent by the comparison client; rejected when given)

post.summary: Local only: move a challenge refusal to the email second-factor step
post.description: Moves a challenge refusal of /v2/register to the email second-factor step (2.26.37.71 launchEmailChallengeFlow). Offline operation; no request sent to WhatsApp.

post.summary: Submit the emailed one-time code from redirected stdin
post.description: Submits the one-time code received via email. Input must be provided via stdin. Completes email verification for registration. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One read-safe /v2/exist probe of method eligibility for the saved attempt
post.description: Probes method eligibility (email one-time code, old-device confirmation, waits). Read-safe; changes no server or local state. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: Validate and show a redacted request plan; no network or store access
post.description: Validates the LabRegistrationConfig and displays a redacted preview of the request that would be sent. Offline operation; no network or store access.

show_phone.description: Explicitly show the configured phone in local output

post.summary: Recheck a saved preflight stopped by the old missing-recommendation guard
post.description: Rechecks a preflight that was previously stopped by the missing-recommendation guard. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: Migrate an opaque legacy refusal using JSON corrections; one send only
post.description: Sends a corrected request after a legacy refusal whose diagnostics were lost. Preserves identity; shares the legacy diagnostic's durable reservation. Single send only. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

post.summary: One retry after bad_token; JSON may change only the token, never identity
post.description: Single retry after a bad_token response. Configuration JSON may change only the token field; identity must remain stable. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

get.summary: Local status only: sends no request
get.description: Shows the current registration attempt status from local state. Offline operation; does not contact WhatsApp.

get.summary: Print the editable profile template; no file, store or network access
get.description: Returns the default LabRegistrationConfig template structure with empty values. Offline operation; no file, store or network access.

post.summary: Submit one OTP from redirected stdin (never a command-line argument)
post.description: Submits the OTP received via SMS or voice. Input must be provided via stdin, never as a command-line argument. Contacts WhatsApp servers.

code.description: One-time password received via SMS or voice

post.summary: Submit one account PIN from redirected stdin; never resets the account PIN
post.description: Submits the account PIN when required for recovery or reactivation. Input must be provided via stdin. Never initiates a PIN reset.

get.summary: Print table counts, journal head, generation and registration status
get.description: Returns inspection data for the protocol store including table row counts, journal state and current registration status. Also reports checkpoint_kinds: a count of Checkpoints rows per leading key segment (for example inbound, received, app-state-key, login-identity). Checkpoints holds many unrelated record kinds under one table, so a bare row count cannot answer whether a given kind is present; only the structural prefix is shown, never the JID or digest that follows it.

post.summary: Create the store (idempotent) and verify the master key opens it
post.description: Initializes the account protocol store if it does not exist, or verifies that the master key can open it. This operation is idempotent.

post.summary: Rotate the master key: re-wrap the data keys under the key found in the given environment variable
post.description: Re-wraps all data encryption keys under a new master key. The old key stops working immediately.

new_key_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the new hex master key

get.summary: Transport wire protocol profile
get.description: Returns wire-protocol profile for transport layer.

post.summary: Onboard a phone number: derive its token, write the private request configuration with the working recipe, generate its master key and profile
post.description: Derives a registration token for the given phone number, generates the master cryptographic key, creates the account profile, and writes a private request configuration with the APK-derived recipe. The token, key and phone are never printed. Files are created with restrictive permissions: 0600 for profile and config files, 0700 for directories. Next step: lab-signup --allow-live-request begin.

material.description: Path to the 2.26.37.70 token-material archive (env WHATSAPP_API_TOKEN_MATERIAL)

dir.description: Base directory for account files (default: lab/accounts/<name>)

get.summary: Get status of registered accounts
get.description: Returns status summary of all registered accounts or a specific account if name is provided. Shows registration state, key availability, pending messages and queued actions.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional account name to filter results (returns only that account if provided)

post.summary: Derive a registration token for a phone number
post.description: Stateless token derivation from APK-pinned material. Derives a phone-bound registration token using the 2.26.37.70 APK material. No state is read or modified. Token is base64-encoded and must be stored securely.

post.summary: Verify that a saved token matches freshly derived material
post.description: Compares the token in a saved request configuration against freshly derived material for the same phone number. Reports match status only; never prints the token or phone. Useful to verify a saved configuration is still valid before sending a request.

config.description: Path to the saved request configuration file

post.summary: Queue a full usync sync of every saved contact (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Register this account's address book with the server using the APK's full/interactive usync mode pair (LX/0u7->A06 envelope, LX/0xX mode-context pairing, both confirmed). This differs from contacts check only in mode and context: check sends query/interactive for a single number, which is discovery rather than address-book registration. allow_mutation is deliberately not emitted because what enables it is unknown. Offline: the request is queued on the durable action queue and a later session transmits it. Whether registering contacts affects Status delivery is unknown and untested; see docs/protocol/status.md.

contacts.description: How many saved contacts the sync includes.

post.summary: Queue a read-only app-state fetch for every collection (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Ask the server for each app-state collection's snapshot at version 0 (CSe.A00/CSe.A01: <sync data_namespace=3><collection name order version=0 return_snapshot="true"/>). Read-only: no <patch> child is emitted, since CSe.A01 adds it only when a patch argument is present. The reply carries the server's authoritative version per collection, which patch writing needs because patches must be strictly sequential. Live 2026-09-22: accepted, and the reply was an empty <sync/>, confirming this account holds no app state.

post.summary: Queue an app-state contactAction patch publishing every saved contact (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Build and queue a SyncdPatch of contactAction SET mutations, one per saved contact, into the critical_unblock_low collection (LX/Azs->A00 routes contactAction there, confirmed — not a 'regular' collection). Index is ["contact", <jid>] and SyncActionData.version is 2, both confirmed from LX/B6M. Mints this device's app-state key if it has none. The <collection version> attribute is the version the client currently holds and is omitted for a never-synced collection (confirmed, CSe.A01 call sites). LIVE STATUS: refused. Two attempts, both answered iq type=error code=400 text=bad-request; the second carried the corrected version semantics. Not iterated further. See docs/protocol/chat-actions.md for the undistinguished candidates.

post.summary: Ask for a new code on the attempt already in progress
post.description: Re-request the verification code for a registration attempt that is already in a pending challenge, because a delivered code expires long before the attempt does. Keeps the attempt id, its identity, its keys and its history; creates no new attempt; honours the challenge handle's retry_after; and refuses any state other than a pending challenge. This is the official client's resend, not a restart.

get.summary: List who has received, viewed, played or liked our statuses
get.description: Offline. Lists the recorded status receipts and likes: who reported, for which status, and how far they got (delivered, read, played), plus any reactions. Receipts are kept at the furthest state a viewer reached, so a delivery replayed from an offline queue cannot demote a view. Reading this sends nothing and emits no read receipt.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only this status, by wire id
